scenes.tts: The first film split life by nuclei and molecular evidence. Which traits can finish the path through Eukarya? Follow the gold branch. Its cells have nuclei, but that trait does not reveal a kingdom.
scenes.caption: The first film split life by nuclei and molecular evidence. Which traits can finish the path through Eukarya? Follow the gold branch. Its cells have nuclei, but that trait does not reveal a kingdom.
scenes.visual: Hook before title. Reuse the first film's pond drop and color map exactly: Eukarya gold; Bacteria blue; Archaea teal; trait evidence white; limits red. The blue and teal paths slide aside while the gold Eukarya path grows to fill the frame.
scenes.narration: The first film split life by nuclei and molecular evidence. Which traits can finish the path through Eukarya? Follow the gold branch. Its cells have nuclei, but that trait does not reveal a kingdom.

scenes.visual: Title only: 'Build the Classification Path'. The gold Eukarya path keeps flowing behind the title.

scenes.tts: A kingdom is the rank below domain. In this course, Eukarya holds protists, fungi, plants, and animals. Ask about cell number, wall material, tissues, and feeding. Answers work together. Familiar appearances can mislead.
scenes.caption: A kingdom is the rank below domain. In this course, Eukarya holds protists, fungi, plants, and animals. Ask about cell number, wall material, tissues, and feeding. Answers work together. Familiar appearances can mislead.
scenes.visual: The gold path passes four large white trait gates: cells, wall, tissues, feeding. Gold cartoon organisms move together toward the gates. Keep fewer than six labelled items visible by replacing each gate as the next arrives.
scenes.narration: A kingdom is the rank below domain. In this course, Eukarya holds protists, fungi, plants, and animals. Ask about cell number, wall material, tissues, and feeding. Answers work together. Familiar appearances can mislead.

scenes.tts: Begin with plants. They have many cells, cellulose walls, and tissues. Most photosynthesize. Fungi can also have many cells and walls, but their walls contain chitin. They digest food outside and absorb it.
scenes.caption: Begin with plants. They have many cells, cellulose walls, and tissues. Most photosynthesize. Fungi can also have many cells and walls, but their walls contain chitin. They digest food outside and absorb it.
scenes.visual: A pine cartoon and oyster mushroom grow from the same gold nucleus icon. White wall bands appear around their cells. The pine receives 'cellulose' and a light-to-food arrow. The mushroom receives 'chitin' and an outside-digestion arrow moving inward.
scenes.narration: Begin with plants. They have many cells, cellulose walls, and tissues. Most photosynthesize. Fungi can also have many cells and walls, but their walls contain chitin. They digest food outside and absorb it.

scenes.tts: Here are an oyster mushroom and a green plant. Both have nuclei, many cells, and walls. Which traits separate their paths better than movement? Choose before the evidence appears.
scenes.caption: Here are an oyster mushroom and a green plant. Both have nuclei, many cells, and walls. Which traits separate their paths better than movement? Choose before the evidence appears.
scenes.visual: Place the mushroom and plant large and side by side on the carried gold path. Three white trait gates appear: movement, wall material, feeding. Keep all neutral. Gentle growth and drifting spores prevent a frozen frame.
scenes.narration: Here are an oyster mushroom and a green plant. Both have nuclei, many cells, and walls. Which traits separate their paths better than movement? Choose before the evidence appears.

scenes.visual: Hold the question and all three neutral gates. A small white progress arc advances without numbers. Do not highlight an answer.

scenes.tts: Movement is unreliable because both may stay in place. The mushroom follows chitin and absorption toward fungi. The plant follows cellulose, tissues, and photosynthesis toward plants. When one familiar trait fails, ask a better one: wall material and feeding settle this split.
scenes.caption: Movement is unreliable because both may stay in place. The mushroom follows chitin and absorption toward fungi. The plant follows cellulose, tissues, and photosynthesis toward plants. When one familiar trait fails, ask a better one: wall material and feeding settle this split.
scenes.visual: The movement gate fades without a red rejection. The wall and feeding gates merge into paired evidence tracks. Chitin and absorption guide the mushroom to fungi; cellulose, tissues, and photosynthesis guide the plant to plants.
scenes.narration: Movement is unreliable because both may stay in place. The mushroom follows chitin and absorption toward fungi. The plant follows cellulose, tissues, and photosynthesis toward plants. When one familiar trait fails, ask a better one: wall material and feeding settle this split.

scenes.tts: Animals have many cells and no cell walls. They ingest food and usually form tissues. Sponges are a special case for tissues. In this scheme, other eukaryotes go with protists. Most are one cell, but some are multicellular algae.
scenes.caption: Animals have many cells and no cell walls. They ingest food and usually form tissues. Sponges are a special case for tissues. In this scheme, other eukaryotes go with protists. Most are one cell, but some are multicellular algae.
scenes.visual: A blue crab enters the no-wall and ingesting gates, then settles at animals. A paramecium and a large kelp cartoon enter the remaining gold route to protists. Add a small 'six-kingdom scheme' scope label beside that route.
scenes.narration: Animals have many cells and no cell walls. They ingest food and usually form tissues. Sponges are a special case for tissues. In this scheme, other eukaryotes go with protists. Most are one cell, but some are multicellular algae.

scenes.tts: Protists vary in feeding. Some make food, some take it in, and some do both. A green, photosynthesizing cell is not automatically a plant. The full pattern matters more than one trait.
scenes.caption: Protists vary in feeding. Some make food, some take it in, and some do both. A green, photosynthesizing cell is not automatically a plant. The full pattern matters more than one trait.
scenes.visual: The paramecium transforms into a green single cell. A light arrow and a food-particle arrow enter it together. One green trait token tries to pull it toward plants, but the nucleus, single-cell, and mixed-feeding tokens keep it on the protist route.
scenes.narration: Protists vary in feeding. Some make food, some take it in, and some do both. A green, photosynthesizing cell is not automatically a plant. The full pattern matters more than one trait.

scenes.tts: The plant branch can divide again. Mosses lack vascular tissue and seeds. Ferns have vascular tissue but no seeds. Both spread by spores. Conifers carry seeds in cones. Flowering plants hold seeds inside fruits.
scenes.caption: The plant branch can divide again. Mosses lack vascular tissue and seeds. Ferns have vascular tissue but no seeds. Both spread by spores. Conifers carry seeds in cones. Flowering plants hold seeds inside fruits.
scenes.visual: The gold plant path transforms through four large cartoons in one position: moss with spores, fern with vascular tube and spores, conifer cone, flowering branch with fruit. Trait labels replace one another instead of forming a list.
scenes.narration: The plant branch can divide again. Mosses lack vascular tissue and seeds. Ferns have vascular tissue but no seeds. Both spread by spores. Conifers carry seeds in cones. Flowering plants hold seeds inside fruits.

scenes.tts: These paired choices form a dichotomous key. Each answer leads to another question or a group. A key works only for its built-in organisms and traits. If evidence is missing, stop rather than guess.
scenes.caption: These paired choices form a dichotomous key. Each answer leads to another question or a group. A key works only for its built-in organisms and traits. If evidence is missing, stop rather than guess.
scenes.visual: Zoom out to show the carried path as paired forks. An evidence card is removed from one route; a red stop sign rises at that fork while the other routes keep moving. Do not show any unsupported placement.
scenes.narration: These paired choices form a dichotomous key. Each answer leads to another question or a group. A key works only for its built-in organisms and traits. If evidence is missing, stop rather than guess.

scenes.tts: Classification continues below kingdom through phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species. A species name has a capitalized genus, then a lower-case specific epithet. Both words appear in italics. Naming records a result; it does not supply the evidence.
scenes.caption: Classification continues below kingdom through phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species. A species name has a capitalized genus, then a lower-case specific epithet. Both words appear in italics. Naming records a result; it does not supply the evidence.
scenes.visual: The branching key narrows into nested labelled blocks from kingdom to species. Then show the blue crab name Callinectes sapidus in italics, with Callinectes lifting to mark the capitalized genus and sapidus settling in lower case.
scenes.narration: Classification continues below kingdom through phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species. A species name has a capitalized genus, then a lower-case specific epithet. Both words appear in italics. Naming records a result; it does not supply the evidence.

scenes.tts: The path can sort the lesson's real organisms. It separates the archaeon, bacterium, paramecium, mushroom, plants, and crab. The plants still match on the main traits, so division evidence finishes their split.
scenes.caption: The path can sort the lesson's real organisms. It separates the archaeon, bacterium, paramecium, mushroom, plants, and crab. The plants still match on the main traits, so division evidence finishes their split.
scenes.visual: The path becomes a simplified evidence table marked 'schematic'. Organism cartoons slide into domain and kingdom rows. Pine and dogwood pause together under identical main-trait blocks until cone and flower-fruit cards separate them.
scenes.narration: The path can sort the lesson's real organisms. It separates the archaeon, bacterium, paramecium, mushroom, plants, and crab. The plants still match on the main traits, so division evidence finishes their split.

scenes.tts: The scheme is simplified, especially for protists and the deepest branches. Its strength is the method: ask useful questions and follow the evidence. Ask traits in order; stop where your evidence runs out.
